steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: The TCP/IP model is a conceptual framework that describes how data is transmitted over a network. It divides network communication into four layers, each with a specific role. Data passes down through the layers when being sent, and up through the layers when being received. | Function: The application layer provides network services directly to user applications. It is the layer that users interact with most directly. It determines what data is sent and how it is formatted for the application. | Function: The transport layer manages end-to-end communication between two devices.
